rules.name: AntiLife
rules.blurb: Conway's Life in negative: swap live and dead and every Life pattern behaves the same.

rules.name: InverseLife
rules.blurb: Has Life-like gliders and oscillators. It is B3678/S23 with live and dead swapped.
rules.author: Jason Rampe

rules.name: Wickstretcher And The Parasites
rules.blurb: Explosive and strobing. Wickstretchers of many speeds and sizes appear, most with parasites clinging on that resize their wicks.

rules.name: Oils
rules.blurb: Explosive; full of wickstretchers, and home to a diagonal c/16 spaceship.

rules.name: Invertamaze
rules.blurb: Builds mazes that swap live and dead on every step. Warning: rapid flashing.

rules.name: Neon Blobs
rules.blurb: Strobing; patterns blow up into glowing, neon-looking blobs.

rules.name: H-trees
rules.blurb: Explosive growth of branching H shapes along the edges of patterns.

rules.name: Fuzz
rules.blurb: Explosive, with solid regions forming in the growth.

rules.name: Gnarl
rules.blurb: Explosive: one live cell is enough to grow an intricate, gnarled pattern.
rules.author: Kellie Evans

rules.name: Snakeskin
rules.blurb: Explosive; the growth fills with snake-like shapes.

rules.name: Solid islands grow amongst static
rules.blurb: Grows rapidly; solid islands form inside regions of static-like noise.

rules.name: Replicator
rules.blurb: Any pattern at all makes copies of itself.

rules.name: Fredkin
rules.blurb: Like Replicator, any pattern copies itself. Also called Replicator 2.

rules.name: Feux
rules.blurb: Explosive; patterns become replicators that blink on and off.

rules.name: Forrest of Ls
rules.blurb: Explosive, though the inside of the growth slowly settles into still shapes.

rules.name: Seeds
rules.blurb: No cell survives a step, yet it explodes. Many small orthogonal spaceships, but most patterns blow up.
rules.author: Brian Silverman

rules.name: Live Free or Die
rules.blurb: Explosive; only isolated cells survive. Rich in oscillators, spaceships and puffers, some stretchable to any size and period.

rules.name: Serviettes
rules.blurb: Like Seeds, no cell survives and growth explodes, weaving patterns that look like fabric. Also called Persian Rug.

rules.name: Iceballs
rules.blurb: Small solid clumps blink on and off; a few grow big enough to start spreading slowly. Also called Ice nine.

rules.name: Life without death
rules.blurb: Cells never die, so growth only spreads, forming intricate flakes and dense ladder wickstretchers. Also called Flakes or Inkspot.

rules.name: DotLife
rules.blurb: Life plus survival with zero neighbours; explosive. The B-heptomino often grows forever here, but it can be tamed into a spaceship.

rules.name: Star Trek
rules.blurb: Has spaceships moving at several different speeds.

rules.name: Flock
rules.blurb: Soups quickly reduce to period-2 oscillators, dominoes and duoplets; a period-14 pre-beehive shuttle is common.

rules.name: Mazectric
rules.blurb: Grows into mazes, like Maze, but with straighter, longer corridors.

rules.name: Maze
rules.blurb: Spreads and hardens into a maze of corridors.

rules.name: Magnezones
rules.blurb: Explosive, with a fluid-like interior in which four kinds of crystal form.

rules.name: Corrosion of Conformity
rules.blurb: Mazectric without S3. Nearly any start burns slowly, eating away at its surroundings like rust.

rules.name: EightFlock
rules.blurb: Flock with survival on 8 added.

rules.name: LowLife
rules.blurb: Life with survival on 1 instead of 2.

rules.name: Conway's Life
rules.blurb: The most famous and most studied Life-like rule; chaotic, with endlessly complex behaviour.
rules.author: John Conway

rules.name: EightLife
rules.blurb: Life with survival on 8 too. Also called Pulsar Life.

rules.name: Shoots and Roots
rules.blurb: Two kinds of growth: orderly, slow shoots and faster, explosive roots.

rules.name: Coral
rules.blurb: Slow, explosive growth with a texture like coral.

rules.name: 3-4 Life
rules.blurb: Long thought a stable cousin of Life, until computers showed most patterns explode. Many tiny oscillators; period-3 ships move straight and diagonally.

rules.name: Never happy
rules.blurb: Explosive but sluggish; growth takes on diamond outlines.

rules.name: Assimilation
rules.blurb: Very stable; growth ends in lasting diamonds, part-filled inside. As in 2x2, block patterns always stay block patterns.

rules.name: Long Life
rules.blurb: Stable, and named for its many simple oscillators with extremely long periods.

rules.name: Spiral and polygonal growth
rules.blurb: Plows crawl along polygon edges, enlarging them and turning corners. One 16-cell methuselah runs 12127116559 generations before settling to period 2.

rules.name: Gems
rules.blurb: Explosive, with many small oscillators of high period and a very slow c/5648 spaceship.

rules.name: Gems Minor
rules.blurb: Like Gems: explosive, with plenty of small oscillators of high period and a slow c/2068 ship.

rules.name: Grounded Life
rules.blurb: Stable; Life plus birth on 5. Life's usual ships fail, and the commonest ship is Glider 3736, orthogonal at 2c/5.

rules.name: Land Rush
rules.blurb: Chaotic growth spreads out and sorts itself into rows like ploughed fields.

rules.name: Eppstein
rules.blurb: Explosive; Life plus birth on 5 and survival on 6.
rules.author: Dean Hickerson and David Eppstein

rules.name: Bugs
rules.blurb: Explosive, with lots of spaceships packed with live cells.

rules.name: Cheerios
rules.blurb: Explosive; objects called cheerios appear amid the chaos.

rules.name: Holstein
rules.blurb: Self-complementary. Froth wears solid regions away from the corners unless edge oscillators hold them. Ships at c/7, c/5, c/4 and c/3.

rules.name: Diamoeba
rules.blurb: Grows big diamonds whose edges churn chaotically; some patterns grow quadratically, and block patterns stay block patterns, as in 2x2.

rules.name: Amoeba
rules.blurb: Chaotic and evenly poised between growth and decay: blobs with turbulent insides and edges that lurch about.

rules.name: Pseudo Life
rules.blurb: Soups look much like Life's, but the glider breaks down, so few Life patterns carry over.

rules.name: Geology
rules.blurb: Chaotic and finely balanced: large live continents in a sea of roughly 50% chaos slowly wear down into islands. Self-complementary.

rules.name: HighFlock
rules.blurb: Flock with an extra birth on 6.

rules.name: 2x2
rules.blurb: Chaotic, with many simple oscillators, still lifes and ships. The name: any pattern built of 2x2 blocks stays built of 2x2 blocks.

rules.name: IronFlock
rules.blurb: Flock with birth on 6 and survival on 8 added.

rules.name: HighLife
rules.blurb: Life plus birth on 6. Behaves much like Life, but famous for a small replicator.

rules.name: Land Rush 2
rules.blurb: Explosive; once mixed up with Land Rush, probably through a typo. Has an orthogonal c/2 ship of period 4.

rules.name: Virus
rules.blurb: Explosive. The T-tetromino becomes a puffer that leaves blinkers behind, a fitting echo of its traffic-light fate in Life.

rules.name: IronLife
rules.blurb: HighLife with survival on 8 added.

rules.name: sqrt replicator rule
rules.blurb: Has a messy orthogonal replicator, hence the name; once called the logarithmic replicator rule.

rules.name: DrighLife
rules.blurb: Life plus births on 6 and 7: the HighLife and DryLife changes together.

rules.name: 2x2 2
rules.blurb: 2x2 with births on 7 and 8 and survival on 8 added.

rules.name: Castles
rules.blurb: Patterns nearly explode before freezing into stable, castle-like forms.

rules.name: Stains
rules.blurb: Stable: most patterns fill in the areas they enclose. Nearby rules, Coagulations among them, usually explode.

rules.name: Day & Night
rules.blurb: Stable and self-complementary: live and dead regions follow the same law. Many patterns with intricate behaviour are known.

rules.name: LowDeath without Death
rules.blurb: LowDeath in which cells never die.

rules.name: Life SkyHigh
rules.blurb: HighLife plus B8 and S6, which explains the name.

rules.name: LowDeath
rules.blurb: HighLife's replicator still works, though it runs a different sequence because of the pedestrian effect of B38/S23.

rules.name: Morley
rules.blurb: Random soups settle very fast. A slow spaceship and a slow puffer are both common. Also called Move.

rules.name: DryLife without Death
rules.blurb: Cells never die, as in Life without death, but growth goes quadratic instead of building ladders.

rules.name: DryFlock
rules.blurb: Flock with an extra birth on 7.

rules.name: Mazectric with Mice
rules.blurb: Mazectric plus B7; mice shuttle to and fro along the maze corridors.

rules.name: Maze with Mice
rules.blurb: Maze plus B7. As in Mazectric with Mice, mice shuttle along corridors that keep lengthening.

rules.name: DryLife
rules.blurb: Life plus B7; explosive. Ships larger than the glider fail, hence the name. A 9c/28 R-pentomino puffer can be combined into spaceships.

rules.name: Plow World
rules.blurb: Explosive; cells never die, and some patterns become wickstretchers.

rules.name: Coagulations
rules.blurb: Explosive; patterns usually spread without end, leaving thick goo. Oddly, it has one birth condition fewer than the stable Stains.

rules.name: Pedestrian Life without Death
rules.blurb: Pedestrian Life in which cells never die.

rules.name: Pedestrian Flock
rules.blurb: Pedestrian Life's births (3 and 8) with Flock's survival (1 and 2).

rules.name: HoneyFlock
rules.blurb: Flock with the extra B8 and S8 that HoneyLife adds to Life.

rules.name: Pedestrian Life
rules.blurb: Life plus birth on 8, with growth patterns all its own and oblique (5,2)c/190 spaceships.

rules.name: HoneyLife
rules.blurb: Pedestrian Life's B8 together with EightLife's S8, both added to Life.

rules.name: Electrified Maze
rules.blurb: Maze with birth on 4 and 5 instead of 3.

rules.name: Oscillators Rule
rules.blurb: Soups dwindle to tiny oscillators and still lifes; periods above 16 are rare.

rules.name: Walled cities
rules.blurb: Stable; pockets of seemingly random activity sit inside walls that keep them apart.
rules.author: David Macfarlane

rules.name: Vote 4/5
rules.blurb: A twist on Gérard Vichniac's voting rule that models majority opinion; also called Anneal.

rules.name: Rings 'n' Slugs
rules.blurb: Activity settles down into the stable rings and slugs that give the rule its name.

rules.name: Vote
rules.blurb: Each cell takes the majority state of its 3x3 block, a simple model of voting. Also called Majority.
rules.author: Gérard Vichniac

rules.name: 9:43 at Knight
rules.blurb: A stable four-state Generations rule.
rules.author: EricG

rules.name: Banners
rules.blurb: Explosive; ships often trail banners that lengthen and flutter.
rules.author: Mirek Wójtowicz

rules.name: BelZhab
rules.blurb: Explosive; shows Belousov-Zhabotinsky-style reaction patterns.

rules.name: BelZhab Sediment
rules.blurb: Explosive; BelZhab-style activity that leaves spreading beds of sediment.
rules.author: Jason Rampe

rules.name: Bloomerang
rules.blurb: Expanding waves bounce back into slow, soft, rounded kaleidoscopic forms.
rules.author: John Elliott

rules.name: Bombers
rules.blurb: Chaotic; a close cousin of Star Wars with many more decay states, full of fine oscillators, ships and puffers.
rules.author: Mirek Wójtowicz

rules.name: Brain 6
rules.blurb: Chaotic; a variant of Brian's Brain for which many patterns have been built.
rules.author: Michael Sweney

rules.name: Brian's Brain
rules.blurb: Chaotic and widely loved: a ready cell fires when exactly two neighbours fire, then rests for a step. Nicknamed Brain or BB.
rules.author: Brian Silverman

rules.name: Burst
rules.blurb: Chaotic; kin to Nova and Prairie on fire. Big regions slowly fade or break into oscillators; named for a typical exploding oscillator.
rules.author: Michael Sweney

rules.name: Burst II
rules.blurb: Chaotic; Burst minus its one-cell still life (no S0). Has ships fast and slow, methuselahs, and a signature oscillator of period 500+.
rules.author: Michael Sweney

rules.name: Caterpillars
rules.blurb: Chaotic, and full of objects that look like caterpillars.
rules.author: Mirek Wójtowicz

rules.name: Chenille
rules.blurb: An explosive six-state Generations rule.

rules.name: Circuit Genesis
rules.blurb: Expanding; grows circuit-like structures that keep developing long after the starting pattern's edges have moved away.
rules.author: Charles A. Rockafellor

rules.name: Cooties
rules.blurb: Explosive and lively; cells swarm about like lice.
rules.author: Rudy Rucker

rules.name: Ebb and Flow
rules.blurb: Slowly explosive, with lively motion inside the growing edge. A pattern's symmetry often decides whether it grows forever or dies.
rules.author: Michael Sweney

rules.name: Ebb and Flow II
rules.blurb: Explosive; a near relative of Ebb and Flow, with simple gliders.
rules.author: Michael Sweney

rules.name: Faders
rules.blurb: Explosive; part Life, part Brian's Brain. Cells are born and keep firing on exactly two firing neighbours, then fade through 23 refractory states.
rules.author: Rudy Rucker and John Walker

rules.name: Fireworks
rules.blurb: Explosive; looks remarkably like fireworks. Random or designed starts both work, and even a few scattered cells run for a long time.
rules.author: John Elliott

rules.name: Flaming Starbows
rules.blurb: Explosive; growing diamonds and skewed parallelograms sweep the grid, trailing fire and spirals, a bit like Faders crossed with Zhabotinsky spirals.
rules.author: Charles A. Rockafellor

rules.name: Frogs
rules.blurb: Chaotic; its frog-shaped gliders are very common and give it its name.
rules.author: Scott Robert Ladd

rules.name: Frozen Spirals
rules.blurb: Cyclic; Zhabotinsky-style spirals whose corners grow icicles.
rules.author: Mirek Wójtowicz

rules.name: Glisserati
rules.blurb: Explosive; simple seeds tend to fill with gliders in kaleidoscopic patterns, though some runs stay sparse, like Transers, with very long transients.
rules.author: John Elliott

rules.name: Glissergy
rules.blurb: Explosive; Glisserati with 5 states instead of 7. That makes it much busier: random and simple starts alike run for a long time.
rules.author: John Elliott

rules.name: Lava
rules.blurb: Expanding; patterns fill in, very slowly, with something like molten lava.
rules.author: Mirek Wójtowicz

rules.name: Lines
rules.blurb: Stable; rapidly sorts itself into straight lines and separate areas of orthogonal hatching. Best from a 20%-dense disc of radius 40 or more.
rules.author: Anders Starmark

rules.name: Living On The Edge
rules.blurb: Highly chaotic; whether a pattern lasts or dies out is hard to predict. Also called LOTE.
rules.author: Mirek Wójtowicz

rules.name: Meteor Guns
rules.blurb: Expanding; most larger patterns become a slowly growing fireball that fires off gliders (the meteors). Still lifes and oscillators are easy to find.
rules.author: Charles A. Rockafellor

rules.name: Nova
rules.blurb: Expanding; solid seeds stream outward in steady, vivid growth whose border geometry depends on the seed's size and shape.
rules.author: Mirek Wójtowicz

rules.name: OrthoGo
rules.blurb: Mostly quiet; glider collisions that spawn orthogonal products arise by themselves.
rules.author: John Elliott

rules.name: Prairie on fire
rules.blurb: Explosive; fire spreads across the grid. Looks best in reds and yellows.
rules.author: Mirek Wójtowicz

rules.name: RainZha
rules.blurb: Explosive; about as simple as a Zhabotinsky-style rule gets. Random starts grow spirals by themselves.
rules.author: Rudy Rucker and John Walker

rules.name: Rake
rules.blurb: Explosive; a Worms variant teeming with rake puffers, ships and growing wings. Collide them to build puffers and ships of any complexity.
rules.author: Brian Prentice

rules.name: SediMental
rules.blurb: A 30% random fill forms stable islands with busy coasts and traffic between them; sparser starts stay thin, denser ones merge into one continent.
rules.author: John Elliott

rules.name: Snake
rules.blurb: Explosive Worms variant. Its 3x3 square and shuttle oscillators combine into many more; a puffer laying shuttles leaves a snake-like tail.
rules.author: Brian Prentice

rules.name: Soft Freeze
rules.blurb: Chaotic, on the edge between frozen and fluid: crystals grow, melt and regrow next to an active phase, seemingly without end.
rules.author: John Elliott

rules.name: Spirals
rules.blurb: Explosive; steady spirals keep unwinding without end.

rules.name: Star Wars
rules.blurb: Explosive; Brian's Brain with added stability, playing out like a space battle. Rich in natural glider guns. Also called MirekGro.
rules.author: Mirek Wójtowicz

rules.name: Sticks
rules.blurb: Explosive; ships drift among a growing collection of sticks.
rules.author: Rudy Rucker

rules.name: Swirl
rules.blurb: Chaotic; separate whirlpools turn in empty space, in two usual sizes (swirlpool and flamewhirl), plus a flame glider whose twin tail flickers.
rules.author: Scott Robert Ladd

rules.name: Thrill Grill
rules.blurb: Expanding; glittering activity moves through and reshapes a grill of live cells.
rules.author: John Elliott

rules.name: Transers
rules.blurb: Explosive and lively; many distinct objects arise naturally and change into one another.
rules.author: John Elliott

rules.name: Transers II
rules.blurb: Explosive; Transers plus S0, with six states.
rules.author: Michael Sweney

rules.name: Wanderers
rules.blurb: Explosive; a near twin of Prairie on fire whose patterns roam about.
rules.author: Mirek Wójtowicz

rules.name: Worms
rules.blurb: Explosive and vigorous; it breeds swarms of worms.
rules.author: Mirek Wójtowicz

rules.name: Xtasy
rules.blurb: Explosive; in a closed grid, simple seeds make kaleidoscopic waves that dwell on X shapes.
rules.author: John Elliott

rules.name: Majority (LtL)
rules.blurb: Stable; each cell takes the majority of the 9x9 block around it.
rules.author: David Griffeath

rules.name: Bosco's Rule
rules.blurb: Chaotic; famous for its hollow spaceships, called bugs.
rules.author: Kellie Evans

rules.name: Waffle
rules.blurb: An expanding range-7 rule.
rules.author: Kellie Evans

rules.name: Majorly
rules.blurb: Expanding; a range-7 rule whose thresholds amount to a majority vote over the 15x15 block.
rules.author: David Griffeath

rules.name: Globe
rules.blurb: An expanding range-8 rule.
rules.author: Mirek Wójtowicz

rules.name: Bugsmovie
rules.blurb: Chaotic; range 10. MCell calls it Bugs.
rules.author: David Griffeath

rules.name: ModernArt
rules.blurb: Chaotic; range 10 with 255 states.
rules.author: Charles A. Rockafellor

rules.name: Factorio
rules.blurb: Semi-stable; range 3 on a cross-shaped neighbourhood.
rules.author: H. H. P. M. P. Cole

rules.name: Coexistence
rules.blurb: Chaotic; needs a weighted neighbourhood.
rules.author: bubblegum

rules.name: Hexagonal Life
rules.blurb: Life-like rule on hexagons: birth on 2, survival on 3 or 4.
rules.note: Name not confirmed on a LifeWiki rule page.

rules.name: Gnarl (von Neumann)
rules.blurb: Gnarl on the four edge neighbours: born with one live neighbour, survives only with none.
rules.author: Kellie Evans

rules.name: Turmite RLR
rules.blurb: Three colours; spreads as an irregular, chaotic blob.

rules.name: Turmite LRRRRRLLR
rules.blurb: Nine colours; its trail fills out an ever larger square.

rules.name: Turmite LLRRRLRLRLLR
rules.blurb: Twelve colours; lays down a winding, intricate highway.

rules.name: Turmite RRLLLRLLLRRR
rules.blurb: Twelve colours; its trail becomes a solid triangle that grows as it travels.

rules.name: Rule 18
rules.blurb: Class 3: Sierpinski-like triangles from one cell, chaotic from random rows.

rules.name: Rule 22
rules.blurb: Class 3: nested triangles from one cell.

rules.name: Rule 45
rules.blurb: Class 3: chaotic, grows lopsided.

rules.name: Rule 54
rules.blurb: Class 4: interacting particles on a periodic background.

rules.name: Rule 60
rules.blurb: Additive: left XOR centre; a skewed Sierpinski triangle.

rules.name: Rule 73
rules.blurb: Class 2: isolated walls separate periodic regions.

rules.name: Rule 105
rules.blurb: Additive: XNOR of three cells; complement of rule 150.

rules.name: Rule 126
rules.blurb: Class 3: Sierpinski triangle with filled edges.

rules.name: Rule 150
rules.blurb: Additive: XOR of three cells.

rules.name: Rule 184
rules.blurb: Traffic flow: particles move right when the next cell is empty.

rules.name: Layered parity
rules.blurb: Each layer outward from the seed is the XOR of its parents: Rule 90 grown on any tiling.

rules.name: Layered sum mod 3
rules.blurb: Three states; each cell is the sum of its parents mod 3: Pascal's triangle mod 3 on any tiling.
